messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: GGIR version 1.5-18
parts:
Dear GGIR users,

GGIR version 1.5-18 is now online, the key updates are:

1. Improved handling of day saving time (DST) in g.part3 and g.part4.
In the older version DST was accounted for in part 2, but not in the
sleep parameter estimates produced with part 4.

2. Sleep period time window detection algorithm HDCZA is now the
default algorithm to use, when a sleeplog is used and a diary entry is
missing for a particular night. Following my recent work it seems that
HDCZA is far superior than L5+/-6hr, so I think it is justified to
make HDCZA the default fall back option
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2018/02/01/257972.

3. pdf generation in part 3 is now optional (argument do.part3.pdf),
this may be useful for slightly speeding up data processing as it
takes a few second to generate the pdf file, which can accumulate if
your process a lot of files.

The first two changes will affect your sleep parameter estimates for
measurements in which the sleep window overlapped with DST, so please
be mindful that your results may not be consistent with past results.

Best wishes,
Vincent

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: GGIR version 1.5-18
parts:
Thanks Vincent for the update,

In regards to the sleep period time detection with the HDZCA algorithm, you say it is worthy to use it when there is a missing diary entry. But, when there is no diary, is it also recommendable to use this new algorithm instead of the L5+/-6 hours?

Best,
Jairo

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: GGIR version 1.5-18
parts:
Hi Jairo,

Yes, if no sleep diary data is available in a study I would recommend
using argument def.noc.sleep = 1, which activates the new HDZCA
algorithm.

It may be worth highlighting that neither of the methods has been
described or 'validated' in a peer reviewed journal article yet. The
article https://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2018/02/01/257972 is
currently under review at a journal.
I added the L5+/-6 hours algorithm to GGIR in 2015 as a quick approach
to facilitate ongoing methodological research.

Best,
Vincent

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: GGIR version 1.5-18
parts:
Just to clarify with regard to point 1 in my e-mail previous e-mail.

The day saving time has always been correctly accounted for in GGIR.
The only thing that was wrong in previous versions of GGIR and is now
corrected are the sleep parameter estimates derived from the two
nights in the year when the time changes forward or backward.
The code naively calculated the difference between sleep onset and
waking up time, without considering the extra hour or the skipped
hour.

Sorry for my earlier message was not clear.

Best wishes,
Vincent
